articles.headline: Graham and Andrews trade identity-based insults in contentious debate: ‘That’s despicable’
keyFacts: Republican Senator Darline Graham and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews traded criticisms during the South Carolina Senate debate on Sunday.
Graham was appointed to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham, and this was the only general election debate scheduled.
Early voting in South Carolina begins on October 19.
body: Incumbent Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) intensified her criticism of Democratic challenger Annie Andrews in the South Carolina Senate debate on Sunday night.

Graham framed her opponent as “the most radical liberal who has ever run for state office in South Carolina” and said she supports progressive policies such as Medicare for All and open borders. She also said Andrews is “a pediatrician who can’t define what a woman is.”

Andrews rejected those characterizations and similarly sharpened her attacks against the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC)’s sister, who was appointed his replacement after his sudden death in July. Andrews framed her Republican opponent as an establishment figure who won’t challenge any of President Donald Trump’s unpopular policies, particularly those relating to the conflict in Iran and high domestic gas prices. Andrews referred to Graham as “the White House’s ambassador to South Carolina.”

Graham also sharply rebuked Andrews for implying she altered her last name in the wake of her brother’s death. The Republican candidate maintained her legal name “had always been Graham,” and she had never used her husband’s, Nordone, on legal documents, according to the Associated Press .

“I told you my opponent was going to call me a socialist, and there she’s done it again,” Andrews said. “She’s been told to come out here and call me Bernie, Ocasio, Mamdani — that’s what’s in her script. But the truth is, my name is Annie Andrews, and there shouldn’t be any confusion about that because, unlike my opponent, I haven’t changed my name recently.”
“My legal name is Graham, it has always been Graham,” the Republican candidate said in response. “Thank you for bringing up a horrible memory for me.”

The three candidates also discussed artificial intelligence and data center construction, the nation’s debt problem, and Social Security . Graham noted in her opening statement this election cycle is the first time South Carolina will elect a woman to the Senate, and the debate occurred exactly three months after her late brother’s death. Libertarian Kasie Whitener was the third participant.

“My opponent has flip-flopped on almost every issue during this campaign to try and hide her extreme, radical, & progressive record from South Carolinians,” Graham said in a social media post following the debate. Trump, who was a close ally of Graham’s late brother, immediately endorsed her after she assumed his position.
DARLINE GRAHAM DEBATE MAKE-OR-BREAK MOMENT FOR TRUMP-BACKED NOMINEE
Sunday’s contentious gathering was a make-or-break moment in the race, given it’s the only general election debate currently scheduled. Early voting in the state begins Oct. 19.

Though South Carolina is a state Trump won in the 2024 presidential election by almost 18 percentage points, Democrats largely view Graham’s seat as a pickup opportunity. She faced criticism following a primary debate in which she said national security “is not my thing” while fielding a question about China and Taiwan, a comment notable in part because of her late brother’s devotion to that topic.

articles.headline: Woltemade & McTominay time! England eyes Sucic, Malen ban: AM☀️
keyFacts: Juventus is preparing to face Celta Vigo in the Europa League while managing a lengthy injury list that excludes multiple players.
Inter rejected approaches from two English clubs for Petar Sucic, who aims to secure a regular starting position with the team.
Donyell Malen is expected to receive a one-match suspension following a red card received in the match against Como.
body: Woltemade & McTominay time! England eyes Sucic, Malen ban: AM☀️ The Serie A matchday concludes today with Monday’s two fixtures, but the league’s biggest clubs are already looking ahead to their cup commitments and the next round of matches.
Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month!
Let’s look at today’s biggest stories.
🚑 Juve’s injury crisis continues! Woltemade ready

Following their draw against Cagliari , Juventus are preparing to return to Europa League action: on Thursday, the Bianconeri visit Celta Vigo , aiming to build on their brilliant European opener, a 5-0 thrashing of NEC featuring five different scorers. However, Luciano Spalletti still has a lengthy injury list to contend with: from Yildiz to Locatelli , along with Boga, Ekhator and Thuram, none will recover in time for the trip to Spain. The only player returning will be goalkeeper Neto, who missed the league match through suspension, while Zhegrova is unavailable because he is not on the UEFA squad list.

The absences pave the way for some changes, particularly in defence, where Gatti and Kelly are hoping to start. In attack, Woltemade ’s situation remains to be assessed: he has already scored against NEC but is still searching for his first Serie A goal. The German failed to impress in the closing stages against Cagliari, but Spalletti could give him another opportunity in Europe, where Juventus want to continue playing a leading role.
😔 Milan, Cardinale disappointed with Amorim

Gerry Cardinale was at the Mapei Stadium for Sassuolo-Milan, reaffirming his support for the team: Sunday’s game was the sixth league match the Rossoneri owner has attended in person. However, according to Sky Sport , the 1-1 draw in Reggio Emilia reportedly fell short of his expectations .

Milan need to show signs of improvement as early as Thursday, when they face Salzburg in the Europa League following their opening defeat to Benfica. Cardinale is reportedly particularly concerned about Amorim ’s attacking approach, with Gonçalo Ramos too little involved in the build-up, as well as their defensive frailties and performances at set pieces. After an extended period of work during the break, a more noticeable step forward was expected from the team: now they need to deliver.
🙅‍♂️ Inter turned down two English clubs for Sucic! But without a starting spot...

Zvonimir Boban ’s comments have reignited the debate over the future of Petar Sucic , who has so far played less than he expected at Inter. The Dinamo Zagreb president praised the Croatian midfielder, calling him one of the best in the world in his position, and questioned whether staying in Milan would be the right move if the situation does not change. However, according to the well-known Croatian newspaper Sportke Novosti , the player is happy with his experience at Inter and is not considering leaving,

His future will depend above all on his playing time over the coming months. Newcastle and Everton had already shown interest in the Croatian, but Inter previously rejected the English clubs’ approaches. For his part, Sucic does not want to settle for a peripheral role: he aims to become a regular starter and would only consider other options if he fails to achieve that.
🔙 Napoli, it’s McTominay’s time!

After their win against Frosinone, Napoli are preparing for Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Villarreal , aiming to build on the progress shown in the league. According to Corriere dello Sport , Allegri is expected to stick with the 3-4-2-1 , but could make three changes to the starting line-up: Scott McTominay , Billy Gilmour and Matteo Politano are in contention to start after coming off the bench in the match at the Maradona.

The tactical setup remains to be finalised. McTominay could partner Lobotka in central midfield or move into an attacking midfield role, with either Lang or Neres at risk of losing their place; Gilmour, meanwhile, could line up alongside the Slovak, giving De Bruyne more freedom in attacking midfield. There are two options for Politano: play on the right of the four-man midfield, with Di Lorenzo dropping back into defence, or take a more advanced position in place of Neres.
🟥 Roma, how long a ban could Malen face?

Donyell Malen received the first red card of his career, sent off against Como for a dangerous challenge on Kaiki . The Roma striker protested over a foul he had suffered moments earlier, but the referee upheld the dismissal. As Luca Marelli explained on DAZN, the decision was correct: the speed of the challenge, the proximity of the knee and the exposed studs are enough to constitute serious foul play , even though there was no full contact.

The expected punishment is a one-match suspension : Malen will therefore miss Saturday’s clash with Genoa , but will be available again for the big match against Napoli. There are no issues, however, for Wednesday’s European fixture against Real Madrid , in which the Dutchman will be free to lead Roma’s attack.
🤔 Lazio heading to the Stadium without organised supporter groups?

The trip to face Juventus has already drawn a strong response from Lazio fans: all 1,016 seats in the lower tier of the away section at the Allianz Stadium have sold out. According to Il Tempo , tickets remain available for the upper tier, which offers another 2,099 seats. The number of Lazio supporters in Turin could therefore increase over the coming days, in contrast to the ongoing protest involving some fans at home matches at the Stadio Olimpico.

However, the position of the organised supporter groups remains unclear, as they have not yet announced whether they will follow the team on the trip. Ticket sales already confirm a significant turnout, but do not yet resolve the question of whether the organised groups will be present at the Allianz Stadium. A decision is expected in the coming days.
🎯 Fiorentina had two big names in their midfield sights

Midfield remains one of the issues Fiorentina need to address. As Corriere Fiorentino points out, the summer plans focused on the quality of Fagioli, Oulai and Atta , but the idea of relying on a technically gifted midfield must be balanced against the need for greater defensive cover and stability. Atta’s injury further complicates matters, with the player set to remain sidelined for some time.

That is why, in the closing stages of the summer transfer window, Fabio Paratici tried to act, sounding out players such as Torreira, Thorstvedt and Brozovic , after Grosso had identified Matic and Hojbjerg as two potential reinforcements. However, no deal was completed and the issue remained unresolved, carrying over from Grosso’s tenure to that of current coach Vanoli . The club must now assess how to give their midfield greater solidity.

articles.headline: Dodgers drop Game 1 of NLCS in Milwaukee
keyFacts: The Los Angeles Dodgers lost 2-1 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday.
Manager Dave Roberts stated that the team will stick with catcher Will Smith despite his recent struggles.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto is scheduled to pitch Game 2 on Monday as the Dodgers attempt to tie the series.
body: Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Will Smith (16) reacts as Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell (5) scores during the fifth inning in game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. MILWAUKEE — The Dodgers had their chances. They had runners in scoring position, chased Jacob Misiorowski from the mound before he could complete five innings, and received three scoreless innings from their bullpen. But when the Dodgers needed one final swing to change the outcome, Mookie Betts came up short.

The Dodgers dropped Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday, falling 2-1 to the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field. The Dodgers now trail 0-1 in the series, and Milwaukee has already accomplished something it couldn't do last postseason: take the opening game and put itself in position to avoid another sweep at the hands of the Dodgers.
With Game 1 decided by a single run, the Dodgers were left to wonder what might have been after repeatedly failing to capitalize on their scoring opportunities.
The final chance came in the ninth inning.

After pinch hitter Josue De Paula worked a walk to put runners on first and second, the Dodgers brought the potential tying run into scoring position. Betts, who led off for the Dodgers with Shohei Ohtani batting fourth, stepped to the plate with an opportunity to extend the game.
Instead, Betts lifted a deep fly ball to center field, ending the game and sending Milwaukee into celebration.
For a Dodgers team accustomed to playing deep into October, the loss was a frustrating start to a series that figures to test both clubs.
"It's going to be a long series. We knew it coming in," Dave Roberts said.
Roberts reiterated that sentiment when discussing Milwaukee's position as the team with the best regular-season record in baseball.
"You can't go into a long series against a team that has the best record in baseball and expect to just win 4. It's going to be a long series, we knew it coming in," Roberts said.
Missed Opportunities Prove Costly
The Dodgers' offense never found the consistent rhythm needed to overcome Milwaukee's pitching.

The Dodgers managed five hits against Misiorowski, who worked 4⅓ innings and allowed one run while striking out five and walking three. The Dodgers eventually forced the Brewers to turn to their bullpen, but the damage never materialized into a comeback.
Andy Pages accounted for the Dodgers' lone run with a second-inning RBI single. Beyond that, the Dodgers struggled to turn baserunners into runs, leaving several opportunities unfinished.

One of the most significant moments came in the sixth inning, when the Dodgers had runners on the corners against Abner Uribe. With a chance to tie the game or take the lead, Pages struck out to end the threat.
That failure loomed large as Milwaukee's bullpen continued to shut down the Dodgers.
The ninth inning offered one final opportunity, but Betts' flyout ensured the Dodgers would leave Milwaukee without a win to open the series.
Skubal Keeps Dodgers in the Fight, but Brewers Take Control
The pitching matchup between Tarik Skubal and Misiorowski delivered the kind of tense October baseball expected from two teams with championship aspirations.

Skubal struck out seven over five innings, allowing five hits, two walks and two earned runs on 81 pitches. Although he escaped a bases-loaded jam in the fifth, Milwaukee eventually found the breakthrough it needed.

Garrett Mitchell opened the inning with a walk before Cooper Pratt moved him into scoring position with a bunt. Luis Lara followed with an RBI single, bringing Mitchell home to give the Brewers a 2-1 advantage.
That proved to be the difference.

Roberts turned to Alex Vesia for the left-handed portion of Milwaukee's lineup after Skubal completed his outing. The Dodgers' bullpen delivered three scoreless innings, keeping the deficit at one run and giving the offense an opportunity to respond.
It was a strong relief effort, but the Dodgers couldn't provide the tying run.
Freeman, Betts Refuse to Panic
Despite the disappointment, the Dodgers were quick to emphasize that one loss does not define a seven-game series.
Freddie Freeman acknowledged the frustration while keeping the team's focus on the bigger picture.
"Any loss in the playoffs is not great, but it's a long series. It's just the first game," Freeman said.
Freeman also expressed confidence heading into Monday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto scheduled to take the ball for Game 2.
"It's just the first game. We'll come back out tomorrow with Yamamoto, I feel pretty confident," Freeman said.
Betts delivered a similar message following his game-ending flyout.
"We got to focus on the task at hand, and that's winning the game tomorrow," Betts said.
For a Dodgers club that entered the postseason with championship expectations, the challenge now is to turn that confidence into a response on the field.
Roberts Sticks With Will Smith
One of the Dodgers' other concerns entering Game 2 is the production of Will Smith.

Smith went 0-for-3 in the opener and has yet to look like his usual self since returning from the injured list. His continued struggles have raised questions about whether the Dodgers might consider giving Hunter Feduccia an opportunity behind the plate.
Roberts, however, made his position clear.
"I'm not going to put Feduccia in place of Will Smith," Roberts said.
The Dodgers are sticking with their veteran catcher, trusting that his experience and offensive ability will eventually translate into better results.
With the series just beginning, Roberts appears unwilling to make a drastic lineup change based on one game.
Yamamoto Gets the Ball With the Series on the Line

The Dodgers won't have much time to dwell on Sunday's defeat. Game 2 arrives Monday afternoon, with Yamamoto tasked with helping the Dodgers avoid falling into an 0-2 hole before the series shifts back to Los Angeles.
Roberts made it clear that he remains confident in his starter.
"They got Henderson, we got Yamamoto. We feel good with our guy," Roberts said.
He reinforced that belief when discussing the urgency of the next game.
"We've got our guy going tomorrow, who we trust undoubtedly. We need to win a baseball game."
The message was straightforward: the Dodgers don't need to solve the entire series on Monday. They need to even it.

Milwaukee, meanwhile, has already secured the result it wanted. After being swept by the Dodgers in last year's postseason meeting, the Brewers have struck first and put the pressure on the defending champions.
The Dodgers still have plenty of baseball ahead of them, but Sunday's loss exposed the importance of converting scoring opportunities when the margins are this thin.

A second-inning RBI single from Pages wasn't enough. Three scoreless innings from the bullpen weren't enough. And a late rally that put the tying run within reach ultimately ended with Betts’ fly ball to end of the game.
Now, the Dodgers turn the page.
Yamamoto takes the mound Monday, and the Dodgers will look to leave American Family Field with the series tied before heading back to Dodger Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday.
As Roberts made clear after Game 1, this series was never expected to be easy.
The Dodgers have their first setback. Their response will determine how much it matters.

articles.headline: New rule, no change - has cricket missed a trick again with bad light?
keyFacts: Bad light caused significant disruptions during the first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban, wiping out over 60 overs.
The International Cricket Council recently amended rules to allow teams to agree to use a pink ball throughout a Test to prevent bad light delays.
South Africa and Australia did not agree to use the pink ball before their match, leaving the new rule unused.
body: - Published
It is one of cricket's oldest and most frustrating problems: bad light.
A fascinating passage of play halted when things get too gloomy.
The issue has reared its head again this week in the fascinating first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban, wiping out more than 60 overs across the first three days.
The fact a solution was added to cricket's rules just last week, an option so far unused around the world, only adds to the frustration.
Bad light in mid-afternoon - what's gone on in Durban?

Play is already starting early, at 09:30 local time in Durban, given this is the first October Test at Kingsmead, a setting where the sun sets shortly after 18:00 at this time of year on South Africa's eastern coast.
Still, on day one, play was halted at 15:23 local time after clouds built. Only 65.2 of the scheduled 90 overs had been bowled and the players were unable to return.
Day two was slightly better with play continuing until 16:25, but that finish was still 35 minutes earlier than it could have been. Day three's end came at 16:31.
On each occasion, the first two sessions have been played in hot, sunny conditions, only for clouds to build in the afternoon - a familiar weather pattern in Durban.

"Very quickly in the morning, as temperatures have risen inland as the sun heats the ground, a sea breeze has formed with winds coming from the sea into Durban," said BBC weather presenter Chris Fawkes.

"This has increased humidity levels through the morning and brought some cloud in. As temperatures have started to fall again towards the evening, this has increased the relative humidity with the air getting increasingly saturated.
"That has caused the cloud to get thicker and lower."
What about the change in playing conditions?
Following a trial earlier in the year, the International Cricket Council amended its playing conditions to allow the pink ball to be used in Tests.
It was supposed to help in these exact scenarios.
Crucially, it does not allow a red ball to be switched for pink when the light becomes poor - something previously suggested by former England captain Michael Vaughan.
Instead, if problems with the light are expected, it allows teams to agree before a Test starts to use the pink ball throughout.
No such discussions were held between the Proteas and Australia before the Durban Test, however.
'There is a stigma around the pink ball'
The pink ball has been a fixture of day-night Tests because it is easier to see than the darker red in night-time conditions.
Former South Africa bowler Shaun Pollock was part of the ICC committee which recommended the change and he believes there is a "stigma" around the pink ball in the game.
"They say it moves too much," Pollock said.
"If Australia were 124-6 [as they were on day one] and we were using the pink ball, everyone would have said it was the pink ball's fault.
"If Australia were 124-6 and got to 390 [as they did in their first innings] everyone in South Africa would have said it was the pink ball's fault, that it got soft.
"The pink ball would have meant we played 45 more overs of Test cricket and that is why I am keen to introduce it, and not just for day-night games."
Why might teams not want to use the pink ball?
One narrative exists that the pink ball moves more under floodlights, though that is not backed up by ball tracking data.
Instead, various batters have spoken about the pink ball being more difficult to see. Batting averages are lowest in the evening of day-night matches.
Australia have also played in 15 of Test cricket's day-nighters - 10 more than anyone else.

Unsurprisingly, the four leading wicket-takers in day-night matches are all Australians. Left-armer Mitchell Starc's haul of 89 wickets in 15 Tests has positioned him as the undisputed pink-ball king.
You would not blame teams if they would rather face Australia with the red ball.
Former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander said he prefers the idea of switching balls during the match if conditions require it, but that would raise questions over the Test's integrity.
Is the potential injustice of one team having to face a pink ball outweighed by the need to get more action of the field?
"They have to take it out of the hands of the players completed and enforce it from the umpires' point of view that the pink ball will become in play when the light has faded enough," Philander said.
"You are always going to have the argument of who is ahead of the game.
"I would like to see the ICC enforce it on to the officials to make that call."

articles.headline: Documents falsified to evade tax on Abramovich's wealth
keyFacts: A BBC Panorama investigation found that accountancy firm Deloitte helped falsify documents to hide Roman Abramovich's wealth and evade taxes.
Leaked documents revealed that assets worth hundreds of millions, including yachts and mansions, vanished from company accounts through backdated paperwork.
Abramovich's lawyers stated he denies evading tax or concealing his fortune and relied on professional advice.
body: - Published
The world's biggest accountancy firm helped in falsifying documents to hide Roman Abramovich's wealth and evade tax, BBC Panorama has found.
Accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (Â£508m) vanished from Abramovich's company accounts.
Deloitte also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch's wealth through the falsification of documents.
Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC, an expert in financial services law, said Panorama's evidence showed the scheme was "straightforward" tax evasion and "it couldn't be more blatant".

Roman Abramovich's lawyers said he denies that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune. They said Panorama provided no evidence he knew about, authorised or directed the falsification of any document and said it was legitimate to rely on advice from professionals.
Deloitte Cyprus said it "acts in compliance with applicable laws".
The findings are being revealed following a joint investigation between BBC Panorama and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

For nearly two decades, Roman Abramovich was the most famous Russian oligarch in the UK, welcomed in London where he bought Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and bankrolled the club's most successful period. But after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was sanctioned by the UK government as an associate of President Vladimir Putin and forced to sell the club.

Abramovich has been reported to be living in Turkey, a safe haven for him because it did not apply sanctions. In the Channel Island of Jersey, Â£5.4bn of his assets remain frozen and a criminal investigation has been going on for four years.
The oligarch's lawyers told the BBC he denies the allegations in the Jersey investigation and says it was "undertaken for political purposes".
Our investigation has uncovered new evidence about the way Abramovich's business empire has been run. It also raises serious questions about the integrity of some of his professional advisers.

The evidence is contained in a leak that includes thousands of documents about the oligarch's finances and the operations of a network of offshore companies administered from Cyprus - which used to be a tax haven popular with Russians - between 1995 and 2022.

The BBC and media partners including the Guardian, Paper Trail Media, the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, and the Cyprus Investigative Reporting Network - as well as the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, external - have been reporting on the leaked files since 2023 as part of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists' Cyprus Confidential, external investigation.

In 2022, Panorama also reported on how Abramovich had made his fortune from a corrupt deal to buy a Russian state-owned oil company in the 1990s, selling it back to the government a decade later for billions in profit. He has previously said allegations of corruption in the deal are false.

The profits from Abramovich's oil deals in Russia were funnelled into a web of offshore companies. They were administered from Cyprus by a corporate services firm called MeritServus, in Limassol, the island's second-largest city.

Until 2005, Deloitte - now the biggest of the "big four" firms which dominate the accounting industry - owned MeritServus. After they split, the two companies worked closely together with Abramovich's associates to manage his global fortune.
The leaked documents from MeritServus reveal some of their practices.
Panorama - Roman Abramovich: How He Hid His Fortune

He was the Russian oligarch who brought his wealth to the UK. But whatâs the truth about Roman Abramovichâs fortune? Panorama investigates the documents that were falsified to hide his wealth and evade tax.
Watch now on BBC iPlayer or on BBC One at 20:00 BST on Monday 12 October.

Our first example of backdated paperwork comes in 2006, after a new law in Cyprus meant that company accounts had to be made public. The new transparency law threatened to expose the secrets of Abramovich's vast wealth.
Deloitte Cyprus had prepared draft accounts for 2003 - but had not yet finalised them - for his Cypriot company Amiscan Investments. The accounts detailed $672m of luxury property.

A mansion in West Sussex, a luxury flat in London and an estate in the south of France were all included - plus helicopters, private jets and a small fleet of boats the oligarch owned at the time, including the $147.5m Pelorus.

To keep them secret, Abramovich's associates and Meritservus decided to rewrite history. They drew up a plan to circumvent the transparency law by transferring the assets to Amiscan's parent company in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), where they could be kept hidden. And they backdated the change by three years to make it look like the asset transfer had happened in 2003.
Deloitte Cyprus reviewed the backdated documents and said they were "adequate" to allow them to remove the assets from Amiscan's accounts.
When the 2003 accounts were signed off by Deloitte in 2006, the homes, planes and yachts disappeared at the stroke of a pen. Only $75,000 of assets remained.
Deloitte signed off the accounts even though the leaked documents show it knew they were completely misleading.

Lord Sikka, professor of accounting at the University of Sheffield, said it was a "violation of a statutory duty" and "pretty scandalous" to misrepresent transaction dates and not to publish true and fair accounts.
Panorama also found evidence that backdated documents had been used in a tax evasion scheme.
This involved another one of Abramovich's Cypriot companies, Kravin Investments, which had almost $2bn in the bank in 2003.
It had been earning large amounts in interest, so Roman Abramovich's company should have been paying tax on that interest to the Cypriot authorities.
But his advisers had another idea to rewrite history.

An email from MeritServus in August 2005 to Abramovich's Russian associates said a plan had been devised after a meeting with Deloitte. "If you agree, it will be necessary to change the financial statements and the accounting records accordingly for 2003 and 2004," the email read.
MeritServus informed the oligarch's Russian associates, that Kravin's "Provisional Tax Assessments for 2005" would be filed showing the company earning no income from the money.
A month later, an associate in Russia emailed in response, "I agree".
MeritServus then created a series of backdated documents which falsely purported to show that Kravin was only holding and investing the funds on behalf of its parent company in the BVI.
This made it look like Kravin did not actually own the money, so it would not be liable for tax in Cyprus.

Deloitte wrote in a September 2005 email that "certain changes will have to be made to the accounts (bank account balances, interest income, profit and loss account)" because of the backdated changes to Kravin's assets.
So Deloitte was apparently advising on the falsification of financial records. The evidence suggests it allowed Abramovich's company to evade millions in tax.

Andrew Mitchell KC told us the scheme was "straightforward" tax evasion. "If it happened in England and it was in the millions, His Majesty's Revenue and Customs would be thinking about a prosecution," he said.

Cypriot MP Christos Christofides said that if tax had been evaded, then "we have to see how we can get our money back and how, if some people are guilty, they have to pay the price according to our law."

In addition to the documents which Deloitte helped to backdate, Abramovich's advisers at MeritServus falsified a third set of records. This involved the oligarch's huge business fortune - more than $10bn - held by a company called Electus Investments in Cyprus.
MeritServus backdated documents to make it look like Electus did not own the fortune.
It used another Abramovich company with exactly the same name of Electus Investments, but this time based in the more secretive BVI, where accounts did not have to be made public.

Emails show that in 2006, MeritServus acknowledged that the fortune was owned by Electus Cyprus. But again it proposed to rewrite the past, this time "to transfer the beneficial ownership to Electus Investments in the BVI" and make it look as though the change had happened three years earlier.

MeritServus signed and backdated documents which falsely purported to show the BVI company had owned the $10bn fortune since 20 November 2003. So when the accounts of the Cypriot company with the same name were made public, it appeared to have assets worth just $145,000.
Roman Abramovich's billions had been made to disappear.

Andrew Mitchell KC told Panorama: "What you take away from it is there are professionals who are prepared to bend and break the rules of their profession and therefore the law. And it looks that they will stop literally at nothing in terms of creating documents."

Vladimir Milov, Russia's deputy minister of energy as Abramovich built his empire and now a critic of the Russian government, said: "For each Russian oligarch or Middle Eastern or African corrupt oligarch, there's an army of Western financial and legal services and PR services providers, who is easily taking money for whitewashing their reputation and making them look normal."

Denying any wrongdoing by the oligarch, Roman Abramovich's lawyers said that he was "not involved in the day-to-day operation of those companies" and that where arrangements were proposed by professional advisers, "reliance on that advice was entirely proper and legitimate".
Deloitte Cyprus said it could not comment on the specific allegations because the documents were more than 20 years old and no longer accessible.
MeritServus closed following the Cyprus Confidential leak.

articles.headline: How Iran's elite forces 'mold the minds of the young cadets'
keyFacts: Two high-ranking Iranian security defectors told DW that a secretive circle of elite officers plans assassinations and abductions of regime opponents.
The defectors stated that intense indoctrination, strict isolation, and absolute loyalty to the supreme leader maintain the forces' compliance.
The Iranian Embassy in Berlin rejected the allegations and the conclusions drawn from them.
body: Omid, whose real name cannot be used, signed up to join Iran's security forces when he was 18 years old and harbored "a deep commitment to my country." At the academy, Omid told DW, cadets were under the regime's control "day and night," from their military training through the daily prayers and speeches.
"They mold the minds of the young cadets," Omid said.

Some of these recruits, Omid said, eventually rise through the ranks of Iran's security apparatus to join an elite cadre of officers who plot missions, abductions and assassinations inside and outside of Iran — and have access to unlimited resources and personnel. And, he said, he attended their meetings.
A defector speaks

When Omid, a burly man who carries scars accumulated during his decades-long service as a commander with Iran's elite special forces, reached out in early 2026, deliberations ensued: Could he have been sent to feed DW misinformation and lies to discredit the broadcaster, whose Farsi service is officially sanctioned in Iran? Could he be trying to harm DW or its Iranian employees?

Over the course of months, journalists from DW's investigative unit and Persian department corresponded with him. Omid shared records and photos of his training, which ranged from sniper practice and surveillance to street fighting, riot control and parachuting courses. He also provided photos and videos, documents and locations of a secret monitoring center and housing compounds reserved for high-ranking members of the Iranian security forces.
United in their absolute loyalty to Iran's supreme leader, he said, a clandestine circle of high-ranking officers plot and execute the murder and abductions of the regime's opponents.

Omid's testimony offered a rare insight into Iran's powerful and opaque security apparatus — and into the lives of the men at the core of the Islamic Republic — allowing DW to piece together a picture of how the regime has maintained deeply loyal forces despite widespread protest movements, international sanctions, rising inflation and recent attacks by its two main enemies, Israel and the United States, that eliminated much of its top military and political leadership.

DW corroborated substantial parts of Omid's account with documents, photos, videos and interviews with experts. An intermediary connected the investigative team with a second high-ranking defector, whose account corroborated key details provided by Omid. Though DW confirmed both men's identities, we are withholding certain details to protect them and their families.
In the past, Iran has gone after dissidents and opposition activists abroad, including journalists.
We asked the Embassy or Iran in Berlin and the Supreme Leader’s Office to respond to our findings. The Supreme Leader's Office did not reply.
The embassy in Berlin declined to address the individual allegations, stating that "the Islamic Republic of Iran firmly rejects these allegations and the conclusions drawn from them."
Prayers and privileges

As a high-ranking member of the special forces, Omid had access to the privileges the regime often bestows upon its own: From financial incentives and lucrative economic contracts for their own enterprises to special housing compounds, with their own mosques, schools and hospitals, where personal satellite dishes are banned and religious observance is enforced.

These privileges have their price, Omid said: "control, nothing but control." Officers are tightly monitored. "You're not allowed to just attend a wedding or travel," he said. "They confiscate your passport; they even decide which schools your children are allowed to attend."

The control extends to soldiers' prospective partners, who are first vetted by the regime. Even then, Omid said, he was not allowed to share the true nature of his work with his wife. That, he said, "really eats away at you."

By separating such agents from regular Iranians, the regime can keep a closer eye on its forces, said Saeid Golkar, political scientist at the University of Tennessee, who has extensively researched the command structure of the Islamic Republic's security apparatus. "They can create peer pressure and indoctrinate much more effectively," Golkar told DW.
And, Golkar said, security forces who are largely segregated from regular Iranians are less likely to balk at using force against their civilian compatriots.
A defector from Iran's intelligence agency

A month into DW's interactions with Omid, an intermediary connected us with another high-ranking defector. The man, whom we're calling Reza, worked with the Information Ministry, Iran's intelligence agency.

Like many who are recruited into the security apparatus, Reza hails from a religious family: He grinned as he showed DW a picture on his phone of himself as a young man, sporting the long beard and turban favored by the devout in Iran.
Many of his relatives, he said, still occupy prominent positions in the Iranian regime.

In the early days, he was an ardent supporter of the regime and would sometimes cry during prayers, he said, knowing that he was serving his people and the Islamic Republic and "might even die as a martyr for Islam."

Reza said he slowly turned against the regime as he witnessed the clampdown on protesters. Over the years, officers have shot, arrested and beaten Iranians protesting the country's deteriorating living conditions and strict "morality" laws.
Nowadays, his hair is cropped short.
'Years serving a cruel system'

On the evening of January 8, amid an almost total internet shutdown, security forces opened fire on Iranians protesting widespread shortages and spiking inflation. The extent of the massacre slowly came to light as images trickled out of the country documenting the regime's atrocities.

Thousands of protesters were killed across Iran. Both Omid and Reza said the mass killings which, human rights organizations report, included the shooting of unarmed protesters in hospital beds — had horrified them.
Indeed, this ongoing brutality ultimately led them to speak with DW.
Omid was adamant that he had never shot at protesters nor ordered his subordinates to do so, although DW is unable to corroborate this.
When pressed, he conceded that he had witnessed the killing of demonstrators.

Reza said the guilt he carried after having "wasted 10, 11 years serving a cruel system" compelled him to speak out despite the risk to him and his family. "The truth is: When your opponent is a regime that doesn't adhere to any moral values, you need to be prepared for anything," he said.
Surveillance and suppression

Omid and Reza discussed secret command centers that are central to clamping down on protests. High-ranking members of all units and agencies gather in a monitoring room where, Omid and Reza say, huge monitors on the walls display real-time feeds from countless CCTV cameras around the capital, Tehran. They say there are other such rooms around the country.

Protest marches are also monitored from above by drones. And, Reza said, "information from forces on the ground and from Twitter, Telegram and other social networks, as well as information obtained through surveillance and interception devices — all this information is collected there."
Plainclothes agents often infiltrate protest groups. Omid said such agents were sometimes used to redirect protest marches to places where security forces lie in wait.
A representative of Iran's supreme leader "had a free hand" in ordering operations from within the command center, Omid said, as well as deciding "how harshly the protesters should be dealt with."

When regular police can no longer quell demonstrations, Omid and Reza said, elite units from the Revolutionary Guard and police, often clad entirely in black, their faces hidden behind balaclavas, are sent in to finish the job.
Human rights organizations have documented the use of automatic and semiautomatic machine guns and even heavy machine guns mounted on top of pickup trucks to clamp down on protests.

"The fact that the security forces are equipped with military-grade firearms that were designed for combat situations, for responding to protests, shows that the killings of protesters in the country are intended," finds Amnesty International Iran researcher Raha Bahreini, the author of a recent report analyzing the regime's chain of command during the 2022 protests following the death of Jina Mahsa Aminiin custody.
The Dakhme 'killing machine'

After months of correspondence, Omid pointed DW to an outwardly unremarkable location in Shahr-e Rey, on the outskirts of Tehran: A prayer hall sandwiched between an occupational therapy practice and a pharmacy. Though the prayer hall is named Beit al Shohada, or the house of martyrs, Omid said many officers call the place Dakhme, meaning crypt or tomb.

Omid described how high-ranking officers met under Dakhme's corrugated iron roof to plot off-the-books operations that bypass government structures. He said he had attended several meetings at Dakhme "where decisions about murder are made: It's a killing machine."

Though Omid insisted repeatedly that he had only attended the meetings because he had been ordered to by his higher-ups and he had never taken part in any of the operations plotted at Dakhme, he listed murders and abductions within and outside of Iran that he said were planned there. DW could not verify these cases but found that some of the people named had indeed died under unresolved circumstances.

Several experts DW contacted knew of Dakhme in connection with a murder attempt on an adviser to a reformist president over two decades ago. Others had never heard of Dakhme. No one DW spoke with could confirm its continued operation.

Experts agree that a facility such as Dakhme is plausible. "The Islamic Republic probably feels more of a need now to have these types of groups," Miad Maleki, a former US Treasury official who until recently designed US sanctions programs targeting Iran, told DW.
Indeed, Maleki said, military operations planned covertly at Dakhme would likely give the regime plausible deniability in cases of killings.
Religious and ruthless

Because of the secrecy surrounding Dakhme, much of the following is based only on Omid's accounts and the rare images DW obtained of religious ceremonies inside the hall. The secret meetings usually kick off under the guise of religious ceremonies and rituals, he said, in a large hall often adorned with green drapes and religious banners. After a communal dinner, only those in the inner circle stay.

Those who remain hand over their mobile phones, which are locked away. Then, Omid said, "seasoned specialists from Iran's special forces and intelligence operation " discuss murder and abductions late into the night.

"For these people, a person's position isn't that important," Omid said. "If they consider someone a threat to the supreme leader of the Islamic Republic, they take it extremely seriously and take action."
After each operation, Omid said, the men return to their respective roles within Iran's security apparatus, until they gather again to defend the Islamic Republic at any cost.

Translation from Farsi by: Farhad Payar

articles.headline: Michael Penix Jr. injury: Falcons QB hurts ribs late in regulation on 'SNF,' says he'll be ready for Week 6
keyFacts: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury from a hit by Tavius Robinson late in regulation during a 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football.
Penix stated he was emotional and unable to play in overtime because the pain in his ribs worsened while sitting on the sideline.
Kevin Stefanski said the team will conduct more imaging and testing, while Penix expressed confidence that he will be ready to play against the Chicago Bears in Week 6.
body: The latest injury in Michael Penix Jr.'s snakebitten career was particularly cruel not only for him but for his team, too. Penix took a hard hit to his ribs late in regulation, knocking him out for overtime of the Falcons' eventual 30-23 loss to the Ravens on "Sunday Night Football."
Here's the hit from Tavius Robinson that caused Penix's injury:

Initially, Penix missed just one play -- the one immediately following the hit -- when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game and found Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain on second and 20. Penix returned and threw a ball away under pressure, and the Falcons punted to end regulation.

The Ravens took the ball to start overtime and produced a touchdown drive that lasted over seven minutes. Cameras panned multiple times to the sideline, where Atlanta's medical staff was working on/examining Penix's right ribs. When Atlanta came out on offense, Tagovailoa entered while Penix had a towel over his head, distraught as he could only watch from the sideline. After the game, Penix said he was emotional because he wants to finish games and is frustrated by how many times he hasn't been able to do so.

"I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt, and I did not feel like I was gonna be able to give our team what we needed to help us win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling, so that's all that happened," Penix said. "I was trying to get out there. [I] feel like if we had the ball first in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as we were sitting, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold."
Tagovailoa found Drake London for 20 yards on Atlanta's first offensive play of overtime, but got picked off by Kyle Hamilton on the next snap.
Though Kevin Stefanski said the team will need to conduct more imaging and testing before establishing a timeline for Penix's return, Penix speaking to the media is a good sign.
"Knowing me, I'mma be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough my career," Penix said. "... I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field."
Michael Penix Jr. injury history

Penix, who missed the first two games of the season, had been a huge reason Atlanta turned its season around from 0-2 to 2-2 and is still afloat now at 2-3. The Falcons have now had four different quarterbacks play this season already: Penix, Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (who started the first two games) and Jack Strand (who relieved a struggling Rush in a 34-3 loss in Week 2).

Penix's ability to push the ball downfield helped free up the running game and make the passing game, mainly through London, come to life. The Falcons would very much like Penix's self-diagnosed availability for Week 6 to be accurate, given how much the team has struggled without him.
The Falcons host the Bears in Week 6.

articles.headline: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald turns the page after difficult loss to 49ers
keyFacts: The Seattle Seahawks lost 32-29 to the San Francisco 49ers after committing four turnovers during the game.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald expressed disappointment with the loss but praised the team's effort and connection.
The Seahawks will next play the Denver Broncos on Thursday to move forward and try to improve.
body: Whenever the Seattle Seahawks play the San Francisco 49ers, it's a showdown for the books. This rivalry has been in place for decades, and it's not going anywhere. Still, Sunday's game seemed even a bit more heated, with the defending Super Bowl champion going up against the undefeated 49ers.

It was close, but the 49ers edged out a victory, 32-29. The Seahawks had four turnovers, including two interceptions tossed by quarterback Sam Darnold, as well as fumbles from running backs George Holani and Emanuel Wilson. So, it was a rough day for Seattle.
Mike Macdonald looks ahead after Seahawks' loss to 49ers
After the game, head coach Mike Macdonald expressed disappointment but was also positive. He pointed toward the team's next game, which is on Thursday against the Denver Broncos.

"We're disappointed. I think our guys played hard. We stuck together," he said, according to the team's official website. "I think we got a tough team. I think we're a connected team. But in terms of playing complimentary football, the way that we want to play here as Seahawks and become the team that we want to become, we're not there yet."

He added, "So, good news is we have a game in four days that we can move forward and learn from and try to grow from. So that's the good news. But we need to grow quickly in terms of complimentary football, definitely taking care of the football. Way too many giveaways at this point in the season."
He added that the players "played incredibly hard," but that they're missing something, noting that "the complimentary piece of what we want to become right now is not there, so we didn't do it."
He also gave the 49ers credit for their performance. Now, the focus shifts to "Thursday Night Football" and the Broncos.

articles.headline: Atlanta Dream scrambling to find WNBA finals venue amid scheduling conflicts
keyFacts: The Atlanta Dream are searching for a venue to host their WNBA finals games because State Farm Arena has scheduling conflicts.
State Farm Arena is unavailable due to a concert and Atlanta Hawks games on the required dates.
The team and the WNBA had not announced a decision on the venue as of Sunday night, according to USA Today.
body: The Atlanta Dream are still searching for a venue to host their WNBA finals games against the Golden State Valkyries after scheduling conflicts ruled out State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta.

The Dream are scheduled to host Games 3 and 4 of the best-of-seven series on 22 and 24 October, along with Game 6 on 29 October if necessary. But State Farm Arena, the 17,044-seat home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks, is unavailable on all three dates.
The arena is hosting a concert by singer Sombr on 22 October and Hawks regular-season games on 24 and 29 October.

Atlanta’s regular home venue, Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Georgia, holds just 3,500 spectators for basketball. The Dream have been exploring larger alternatives, including the 13,000-seat Gas South Arena in Duluth and Georgia Tech’s 8,600-seat McCamish Pavilion, but have yet to secure an agreement, USA Today reported.

Dream president and chief operating officer Morgan Shaw Parker said last week that the team were “finalizing details on their home venue and where we will be playing”. The team and the WNBA had not announced a decision as of Sunday night.
Atlanta played six of their 22 regular-season home games at State Farm Arena this season and hosted all three of their previous home playoff games there, averaging 9,695 fans.

The Dream announced last week that they will move to State Farm Arena full-time beginning in 2027 under a multi-year agreement. The move coincides with the WNBA’s expansion to a 50-game regular season, giving Atlanta 25 home dates.

Golden State, meanwhile, will host Games 1 and 2, along with Games 5 and 7 if necessary, at the 18,064-seat Chase Center in San Francisco. The Valkyries have sold out every home game this season, becoming the first women’s professional sports team to exceed $100m in annual revenue.

The WNBA has previously staged finals games at alternate venues because of scheduling conflicts. Atlanta hosted a game during the 2013 finals at what is now Gas South Arena, while the Washington Mystics played three games of the 2019 finals at their 4,200-seat home arena.
The Dream are making their first finals appearance since 2013 after sweeping the Mystics in the first round and the 2024 champion New York Liberty in the semi-finals.
Atlanta have reached the finals three times previously, in 2010, 2011 and 2013, but have never won a game in the championship series.

articles.headline: 66 Years Later, Alfred Hitchcock’s Most Perfect Thriller is Officially Streaming on Netflix
keyFacts: Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller film Psycho is officially streaming on Netflix.
The movie follows a woman named Marion Crane who steals cash from her real estate office employer and goes on the run.
Polygon stated that the film remains entertaining and keeps viewers guessing despite its age and famous twists.
body: Sometimes, when you finally watch some great, important, landmark film for the very first time, the experience of actually sitting down to absorb it doesn’t quite live up to all the hype. Maybe you can appreciate its place in cinema history or whatever, but that doesn’t mean it’s actually all that entertaining (I kind of felt this way about Charlie Chaplin’s City Lights). With the disadvantage of time and the advancement of modern pacing and filmmaking techniques, some classics just don’t hold up.
Psycho is not that kind of classic.

Especially for a first-time viewer, Alfred Hitchcock’s 1960 horror masterpiece is still wildly entertaining and keeps you on your toes throughout the entire picture, which is why, if you’ve never seen it before, it's worth finally watching while it's on Netflix.

Psycho begins with a Phoenix woman named Marion Crane (Janet Leigh), who is in love with a deeply indebted man from Fairvale, California, named Sam Loomis (John Gavin). She has only brief encounters with him while he’s on his business trips to Phoenix, despite them both yearning for more. As long as Sam has so many money problems, he won’t marry her.

Working at a real estate office, Marion sees an opportunity when a rich man comes in and pays for a house in cash ($40,000, representing one of the few things about the movie that does age poorly thanks to inflation). Marion has been instructed by her boss to bring the cash to the bank, but she pockets it and goes on the run, determined to pay off Sam’s debts and live happily ever after with him.

On her way from Phoenix to Fairvale, Marion is deeply worried about getting caught. After an encounter with a police officer where she acts very suspiciously, she decides to switch out her car for a new one, then she continues on. When she gets tired, she decides to sleep a night at the Bates Motel, a remote establishment run by a strange, shy man named Norman Bates (Anthony Perkins). Marion mentions that she’s hungry, and Norman runs back to his house, which sits on a hill behind the motel, and makes her a sandwich, while also being berated with insults from his mother offscreen. Norman then returns to Marion and the two talk in the parlor, which is connected to the front office. They discuss his hobby as a taxidermist and he hints at a dysfunctional relationship with his mother. After the conversation, Marion returns to her room, which is right next to the office. That's when we see Norman spying on her as she undresses.

I’ll stop there, to preserve the experience, in the slight chance that you don’t know what happens next, but even if you do know what’s coming, Psycho is still full of surprises. If there's anything wrong with Psycho, it's that it's become famous and has so many iconic moments — from the shower scene to the twist with Norman's mother — that even without ever seeing it, people may feel like they already have.
But trust me, if you haven’t seen Psycho, you have no idea what you're in for.
Psycho is good, even if you know what’s coming

While, yes, a lot of the big twists in Psycho are spoiled by its fame, the story itself isn’t given away by those iconic moments. I first saw the movie years ago. I watched it again when it just returned to Netflix, I’d forgotten just how many times the movie completely changes what it is. It begins as a movie all about Marion, then the focus shifts to Norman, then this happens a couple of more times. Throughout the movie, Hitchcock keeps reinventing the story by changing the protagonist and going in unexpected directions. So even if you know some of the big reveals of the movie — which you likely do — Psycho still manages to keep you guessing.

All of the different perspectives are interesting, too. A story about a woman stealing some money from her boss may not sound like the most exciting thing ever, but Janet Leigh’s performance is captivating, and you can’t help but wonder if she’ll be caught. We don’t get to the Bates Motel until about a half hour into the movie, but that first half hour still draws you in and could have been a movie all its own. It never feels like you’re waiting to get to the good stuff because it’s all the good stuff.

The movie is helped a ton by its score, and I’m a guy who hardly ever notices a movie's score. Sure, for something like Jaws I can appreciate the score, but usually, I don’t ever think about it. For Psycho, it’s impossible not to think about the score because the movie’s opening titles explode with Bernard Herrmann’s bold string orchestra, which immediately pulls you in and doesn't let go through to the very end. Psycho is a definitive thriller — maybe the definitive thriller — thanks to its still-modern pacing and the way it keeps you guessing, but much of that pacing feels like it's the music doing a lot of the work. It feels as though the music is propelling the movie forward, rather than simply complementing it.

Seriously, put on Netflix and just start Psycho. You’ll immediately be drawn in by that music. From there, Hitchcock tells a story that keeps twisting and changing in unexpected ways, even if you think you know what to expect. While some of the great masterworks of motion picture history are more for “appreciating” than enjoying, Psycho is simply not that kind of classic.

articles.headline: Steam Week in Review: The curious case of Wonder Boy in Monster Land's dubious PC debut
keyFacts: A suspicious Steam port of the classic arcade game Wonder Boy in Monster Land was released by developer Retro Maniac.
Fans and original game composer Shinichi Sakamoto raised concerns that the Steam listing is an unlicensed ROM running in an emulator.
Valve and Sega have not yet responded to inquiries, and a formal DMCA takedown notice has not yet appeared on the Steam page.
body: Wonder Boy in Monster Land released in Japanese arcades in 1987 and for the Sega Master System the following year. Its success led to numerous ports, including to ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64 and Atari ST. Oddly, it never received an official PC port, though that long absence appeared to have come to an end on September 28.
Did fans rejoice? Not really.

The Steam listing for Wonderboy in Monster Land raises one immediate red flag: note the rookie error of "Wonderboy" versus Wonder Boy. The developer and publisher is Retro Maniac, whose only other Steam game is Street Hoop, or Street Slam, an old Data East arcade game from 1994.

To bring you up to speed: LAT Corp owns all IP and assets once belonging to Westone Bit Entertainment, the creators of the original Wonder Boy games. But at the same time Sega, confusingly, owns the Wonder Boy trademark. In other words: LAT Corp owns the games, Sega owns the name. Both parties would need to OK any Wonder Boy re-release bearing the Wonder Boy name.

While the "Wonderboy" misspelling is damning, a Wonder Boy game appearing on Steam without SEGA or LAT Corp prominently displayed isn't unusual. Wonder Boy Returns Remix, which is a "remake" of the original Wonder Boy, lists CFK Co., Ltd as developer and publisher. Not only was it officially licensed, but series creator Ryuichi Nishizawa was involved. Meanwhile, Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap is a thorough remake of the 1989 Master System original, developed by Lizardcube and published by Dotemu. It's also officially licensed. Each listing discloses as much in the Steam page fine print which appears under system requirements.

There's also the wider confusion around the name Wonder Boy itself, which reared its head with the release of Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom in 2019. Since rights to Wonder Boy games are split between LAT Corp and Sega it's necessary to get an OK from both to publish a Wonder Boy game with a Wonder Boy name. But what if you can only get the blessing of one? This dynamic was in play with Monster Boy, which is definitely, spiritually a Wonder Boy game—it had Nishizawa's handprints all over it—though publisher FDG Entertainment didn't license the Wonder Boy name from Sega, hence the name.
To confuse matters even more, the original arcade version of Wonder Boy released as Adventure Island in the United States, spawning a parallel line of unrelated follow-ups.
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

So what is a Wonder Boy game, then? Very few but diehards know off the top of their head, and if this new arcade "port" is illegitimate, it's probably released with full knowledge that this confusion will help it fly under the radar.

I wouldn't have thought twice about it if it weren't for the Wonder Boy Universe fan account on X, which raised the alarm on September 28. Composer on the original game, Shinichi Sakamoto, also weighed in, agreeing that the Retro Maniac port is illegitimate while pointing out that it's not available in Japan. (Sakamoto also claims it's been downloaded 10,000 times on Steam, though I don't know where he got that figure).

Against my better judgement I bought and downloaded the alleged illegitimate version of Wonderboy in Monster Land, and can confirm it's simply a ROM running in the MAME arcade emulator (I've since requested a refund, which was issued promptly). The one obvious change is that a splash screen bearing the Sega logo has been removed.
The splash screen for the Retro Maniac version
The splash screen as depicted by YouTube channel Retro Fighters, playing an arcade ROM
(There's another variation depicted here, only Monster Land is in English rather than Japanese. The SEGA logo remains).

I reached out to Valve about the listing but didn't hear back. I also reached out to Sega several times but received no response. The Wonder Boy Universe X account claims the Retro Maniacs listing is "in the process of being DMCA'd by officials". Presumably they have a direct line to Sega or LAT that I don't have, because only Sega or LAT can file a DMCA. According to Valve's own documentation a DMCA complaint is processed in a maximum of 72 hours but can take longer if the situation is more complex.

Complex or not, Valve's documentation also shows what happens if your listing has a DMCA filed against it. Importantly, a public-facing notice will appear on the Steam page reading "A DMCA takedown notice has been filed on this item". That is yet to happen with Retro Maniac's listing.

This kind of thing happens a lot on mobile storefronts, especially for abandonware. But Wonder Boy in Monster Land isn't, at least strictly speaking, abandonware. I can't say I'm especially worried for Sega or LAT: it's obviously legally wrong for Retro Maniac to upload and profit from a game it didn't make or license—assuming that is the case—but Sega and LAT do themselves no favours by not having legitimate versions of Wonder Boy games easily available on Steam. Monster Lair and Monster World (but not Monster Land) used to be available as part of the SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics collection, but that was removed from Steam in 2024.

Still, it's pretty funny how easily one can simply upload a rip off Wonder Boy game on Steam in 2026. A fortnight after its initial launch, Wonderboy in Monster Land is still officially available, and enthusiasts continue to wonder whether they should support it or not.
Top Steam games by revenue (September 29 - October 6)

That an effortful-looking MMORPG should hit number one in its launch week is unsurprising if you've been following PC gaming for the last quarter century. Also unsurprising is that it's currently sitting on "mixed" reviews. MMOs rarely or never launch to near-unanimous customer satisfaction, and the case against Aion 2 seems to be that it's structured like a free-to-play mobile game. The monetisation is apparently deep-rooted and endlessly distracting.
(I also wonder if NCSOFT will bother employing a proper artist to replace Aion 2's AI-generated assets. Surely you've got the cash?)

It's noteworthy that Minecraft Dungeons 2 only reached number ten during its first full week on sale. It's a Minecraft game, after all. It did launch onto Xbox Games Pass, and it's probably a better performer on console, but it still feels like a humble showing for an offshoot of one of the biggest games in the world.

I also expected Nivalis Nights to factor higher in the list: it came in 27th, though this chart doesn't paint the full picture since the game released on September 30 and thus is handicapped by a day.
Last week's Steam deep cuts
Car Park Capital | October 9

Who needs parks, places to live, shops etcetera, when the land they inhabit would be better served by a car park? That's the dystopian premise of Car Park Capital, which has you destroying the world with vast stretches of yellow-lined tarmac. In addition to turning the world an ashy shade of grey, you'll also need to convince people that they like it. Sounds familiar.
Silver Pines | October 9

Silver Pines is a sidescrolling, rotoscoped horror with the structure of a metroidvania. You're a PI sent to a rundown small town to find missing rock musician Eddie Velvet. Naturally, this small town is not a cheerful and tranquil place, and it's your job to survive its many and varied horrors in pursuit of Velvet. Ammo is scarce, save points are monetised, and the player-character is easily exhaustible. People are calling it Lynchian, but it's not that tonally askew.
Truckful | October 10

Here's a neat 'n' quiet driving game starring a big red truck and a world full of oddballs. As you navigate your lil' Tonka through a colourful and pastoral landscape you'll pick up deliveries to make to the next town, which will fund upgrades to your carriage's carrying capacity. Don't write Truckful off as yet more cosy whimsy: there are mysterious, possibly malevolent forces at play in some pockets of the world.
Buitopia DVD | October 10

As the name kinda implies, Buitopia DVD takes place entirely in the menus of a DVD. And not only that, it was actually built for DVD: you can download the files, burn it to a disc, and experience it in its authentic environment. But what is it? "A game about nostalgia, escapism and what lurks inside 'dead' physical media," reads the Steam description. It has some arrestingly bizarre pixel art.

Shaun Prescott is the Australian editor of PC Gamer. With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. He thinks Lulu by Metallica and Lou Reed is an all-time classic that will receive its due critical reappraisal one day.

articles.headline: Talarico discusses flu absence in multiple exclusive interviews as GOP sharpens attacks
keyFacts: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico stated in interviews that his 13-day absence from campaigning was due to the flu.
Republican opponent Ken Paxton and President Donald Trump criticized Talarico's disappearance and questioned the truthfulness of his illness.
Early voting in Texas begins next Monday, and the midterm elections will be held on November 3.
body: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico discussed his recent absence from the campaign trail for the first time in exclusive interviews on Sunday.

The Texas state representative was spotted in public on Friday at the Austin City Limits Music Festival after not campaigning for almost two weeks. He attended the Kacey Musgrove concert in Dallas on Saturday night before addressing speculation about his lengthy disappearance in interviews released on Sunday afternoon.

“I was at home sick in bed with the flu,” he told the Dallas Morning News in an exclusive interview with its editorial board, in which he says he’s “running as a moderate” and discusses his views on religion, healthcare, and education. Talarico, who suffers from Type 1 diabetes, added that he took a break from campaigning to ensure the sickness wasn’t prolonged.

“I had the flu. This is the craziest thing I’ve ever heard,” he said separately in an interview with MS Now , referencing widespread speculation that this explanation for his absence wasn’t sound. “It’s wild that someone can just post something on the internet and people just run with it.”

Talarico’s Republican opponent, Texas State Attorney General Ken Paxton , spent much of the latter half of last week arguing that Talarico’s disappearance renders him unfit for office. He started a “Where is James Talarico?” chant at a campaign rally on Wednesday and said on Saturday, “He owes Texans answers.”

“James Talarico will not face up to his actual record and tell the people the truth, so I don’t know whether to believe him about the flu or not,” he said on Sunday night in an interview with Fox News . “I just know that everything that he says, almost everything that he says, has been false since the beginning of this campaign.”

President Donald Trump also slammed Talarico last week for not interacting with voters this close to the midterm elections. He referenced the controversy at a rally in Tennessee on Saturday night, saying “he has the longest flu ever recorded.” Talarico holds a slight lead over Paxton, according to public polling, despite Texas’s history as a Republican stronghold.

Paxton also said his campaign has been “working with him on that for months” when asked about the possibility of debating Talarico. The Democratic candidate referenced the pair’s inability to find a time to debate in a Saturday night social media post.
I challenged Ken Paxton to a debate 85 days ago, but no one has heard from him.
People are getting worried.
I’ve received credible reports he's suffering from a rare condition that causes clinical levels of cowardice. @KenPaxtonTX : I am asking for proof of ability to debate.
— James Talarico (@jamestalarico) October 10, 2026
TALARICO SPOTTED IN PUBLIC AFTER 13-DAY ABSENCE FROM CAMPAIGN TRAIL

“And of course we can never quite work out the details because he always wants something we can’t do,” Paxton continued. “So the reality is the big story is the fact that he was missing from the campaign trail, and I know he’d love to change the topic to debates, but the big story is two weeks is a very long time to be away with the flu, and it’s just a very strange time to disappear.” Early voting in Texas begins next Monday, while the midterm elections will be held on Nov. 3.
Talarico also told NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth on Sunday his symptoms were “nothing worse than a nasty case of the flu.”
